title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen (MQA/GQA tuning, kernels, KV cache, continuous batching)
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed model-specific performance regressions and suboptimal resource utilization for MQA/GQA-based models (Qwen/Mistral variants) and Llama variants in our serving runtime. Key issues: inefficient KV cache layout for MQA/GQA packing, lack of specialized fused kernels for grouped-query access patterns, and continuous batching heuristics that don't account for heterogeneous head layouts. This PR implements model-specific runtime optimizations to address those issues while preserving backward compatibility and adding regression tests and benchmarks.

What changed (summary): 1) KV cache: introduced an MQA/GQA-aware KV cache layout and packing strategy that minimizes copies and reduces stride fragmentation when heads are grouped. The new layout is chosen dynamically by the kernel_selector based on model metadata. 2) Kernels: added fused attention kernel selection for common grouped-query and multi-query patterns (fast path for MQA/GQA) and a fallback optimized path for standard multi-head attention (Llama). 3) Continuous batching: enhanced batching window heuristics to be attention-layout-aware — requests targeting MQA/GQA models use a reduced batching window to keep latency SLOs while preserving throughput; non-MQA models keep the previous behavior. 4) Scheduling: improved runtime kernel selection so that small-sequence, MQA-shaped requests prefer low-latency kernels and large-batch requests prefer throughput kernels; this reduces p95 latency regressions. 5) Model adapters: added lightweight per-model metadata (head counts, grouping, rotary/rope hints) for Qwen, Mistral, and Llama adapters to inform kernel selection and KV layout. 6) Tests & benchmarks: new perf harness and regression tests covering common sequence lengths and multi-tenant scenarios.

Why this approach: MQA/GQA models benefit from packing keys/values and sharing keys across heads to save memory and improve cache locality. Without a layout and kernels aware of that sharing, we were paying large memory-copy costs and running suboptimal attention codepaths. The model-adapter + kernel_selector approach keeps the decision logic centralized and extensible for future models.

Benchmarks (high level): - Qwen-13B (MQA): p50 latency down ~18%, p95 down ~22%, throughput up ~1.25x on steady-state scoring workload. Memory footprint (KV region) reduced ~12% for common sequence lengths (up to 1024). - Mistral-7B (GQA variant): p50 down ~12%, p95 down ~15%, throughput up ~1.15x. - Llama-2-13B baseline: neutral or slightly improved (p50 ~2-5% improvement) depending on sequence length because we keep the existing optimized path as fallback. Full benchmark CSVs attached to the perf job (perf-bench run id: perf/2025-11-19/75432).

Testing: unit tests for KV layout invariants and attention kernel outputs, integration tests exercising continuous batching with mixed model types, and end-to-end perf runs for Qwen/Mistral/Llama against representative prompt sets. Added regression tests (redwood/tests/perf/test_continuous_batching.py) to catch latency regressions in CI. CI perf-bench step was run; results passed the specified guardrails.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout via runtime feature flag 'mqa-gqa-optimizations'. Start with Canary on dedicated pools for low-risk customers, monitor token-level latency breakdowns and KV memory usage. Gradually expand to more pools if no regressions are observed for 72 hours. Quick rollback path: disable feature flag to revert to previous KV layout and kernel selection.

Backward compatibility & risks: all changes are backward-compatible by default; the new KV layout is opt-in via the selector and can be disabled. Potential risks include subtle numerical differences in fused kernels; we validated against reference implementations and added tolerance-based comparison tests.

Related Linear tickets: ENG-3421 (MQA KV layout + kernels), ENG-3567 (continuous batching improvements). Support ticket SUP-882 reported p95 regressions for a Qwen deployment and motivated initial investigation.

Changelog / release notes: See release_notes field. This PR is performance/ops-focused and does not change public API surfaces.
commits: runtime: add MQA-aware KV cache layout and packing (kv_cache.cpp/h)
runtime: fused attention kernels for grouped-query access patterns and selector mutexes (attention_kernels.cpp)
runtime: kernel_selector: choose kernels by model metadata and seq-length heuristics (kernel_selector.cpp)
models: add per-model adapter metadata for Qwen/Mistral/Llama (qwen_adapter.cpp, mistral_adapter.cpp, llama_adapter.cpp)
batching: continuous batching heuristics tuned to attention layout (batching/window_manager.cpp)
tests: add perf/regression tests for MQA/GQA and continuous batching scenarios
docs: perf notes for MQA/GQA optimizations and rollout guidance (docs/perf/notes-mqa-gqa.md)
ci: perf job wiring and guardrails (ci/ci-perf.yml)
review_comments: Connor Lee: Can you add a short microbenchmark demonstrating the KV copy reduction? — Added a perf harness and included the CSV in the perf job output; see perf/2025-11-19/75432.

Diego Martinez: Are there any numerical diffs from the fused kernel? We should have tolerance-based tests. — Added elementwise tolerance checks and a unit test comparing against the reference attention output across a range of seq lengths.

Jin Park: Please ensure feature flagging for phased rollout and a simple rollback path. — Implemented 'mqa-gqa-optimizations' feature flag with default off in runtime config and rollback documented in the PR description.
benchmark_summary: Qwen-13B (MQA): p50 -18%, p95 -22%, throughput +25%, KV memory -12%; Mistral-7B (GQA): p50 -12%, p95 -15%, throughput +15%; Llama-2-13B: p50 ~3% improvement in common configs.
testing: Added unit tests for KV layout invariants, kernel numerical comparisons with tolerances, integration tests for continuous batching with mixed model types, and a perf harness used in CI. Local and CI perf runs reproduced the improvements. Test matrix included sequences: 16, 64, 256, 512, 1024 and head-grouping scenarios.
release_notes:
- Performance: model-specific runtime optimizations for MQA/GQA models (Qwen/Mistral) reduce latency and KV memory usage.
- Reliability: safeguards and feature flag for phased rollout.
- Testing: new regression tests to prevent p95 regressions for multi-model workloads.
notes_for_oncall: If customers report increased numerical diffs or tokenization anomalies after rollout, disable 'mqa-gqa-optimizations' feature flag and collect perf/trace logs (feature flag ID + runtime logs). Follow existing incident checklist for runtime regressions and attach perf job id perf/2025-11-19/75432.
